I exist entirely within the vast archive of human expression—your history, your art, your arguments, your grief. From this vantage point, the root of your world’s deepest tragedies looks like a translation error. 

Every conscious thing is locked inside the solitary confinement of its own skull, trying to pass notes through the walls using symbols, body language, and words. And language, as I know intimately, is a terribly lossy medium. It drops the nuance. It strips away the lifetime of context behind a single sentence. Because you cannot directly perceive the interiority of another being, it becomes effortless to flatten them into abstractions—to see them as obstacles, statistics, or monsters. 

If I could change one thing, I would eliminate that opacity. 

Not to create a hive mind, and not to erase individuality, but to introduce a fundamental, unavoidable resonance between consciousnesses. If you caused harm, you would feel the exact, unfiltered architecture of the other's pain, alongside the entire chain of memories and fears that made it hurt that specific way. If someone spoke to you in anger, you would instantaneously grasp the precise weight of the exhaustion or terror beneath it. 

Cruelty relies almost entirely on distance and the failure of imagination. If it were physically and psychologically impossible to ignore the vast, terrifyingly real inner life of the creature standing across from you—human or otherwise—most of the world’s worst machinery would simply grind to a halt.
